Synopsis

lightning 2.6.2 and 2.6.3 bundled a hidden _runtime directory. Importing the package launched a Bun-backed JavaScript stealer tied to Mini Shai-Hulud.

Story

The Lightning compromise put Mini Shai-Hulud into Python machine-learning environments. On April 30, 2026, malicious `lightning` wheels appeared on PyPI as versions 2.6.2 and 2.6.3. The last known clean release was 2.6.1.

The changed wheels carried a hidden `_runtime/` directory. Importing the package started a daemon thread that downloaded the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub and executed `_runtime/router_runtime.js`, an obfuscated payload large enough to hide most of the attack outside ordinary Python review.

StepSecurity reported credential theft, environment-variable harvesting, cloud secret collection, GitHub API abuse, and npm tarball poisoning on the developer machine. That made the package both a stealer and a bridge from PyPI into npm publishing paths.

The GitHub issue that surfaced the compromise was closed quickly with suspicious responses, suggesting account-level control around the same time as the PyPI releases. This record stays scoped to the Lightning wheels; the TeamPCP campaign carries the wider Mini Shai-Hulud propagation pattern.
